title: A whole-invoice discount is shared by the size of each side
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Location-A}'s Shop Supplies Charge is 0%, and nothing else is invoiced at {Location-A} today.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced; it has one labor line of 6.00 hours at $100.00 an hour ($600.00), one part sold at $400.00, shop supplies typed by hand as $30.00 and a whole-invoice discount of $50.00 (not on any line); Labor reads {Sales-rep-A} and Parts reads {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Invoice {Work-order-1}.
  2. Open Reports > Sales By Representative, set the date range to today, turn Show Unassigned on and turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  3. Read {Sales-rep-A}'s Labor row for the invoice.
  4. Read {Sales-rep-B}'s Parts row for the invoice.
  5. Add the two rows' subtotals.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice total before tax is $980.00 (600.00 + 400.00 + 30.00 − 50.00).
  • Step 2: two rows show for the invoice.
  • Step 3: Labor row: Labor Invoiced $600.00, Shop Supplies $30.00, its share of the discount ($30.00) (600 ÷ 1,000 × 50), subtotal $600.00.
  • Step 4: Parts row: Parts Invoiced $400.00, its share of the discount ($20.00) (400 ÷ 1,000 × 50), subtotal $380.00.
  • Step 5: $600.00 + $380.00 = $980.00, the invoice's total before tax.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10890; story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative); PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 8 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R6, read 19 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. The build is not yet available to check this case against.

The Sales By Representative spec, version 28 (12 Oct 2026, S5-R11), still keeps whole-invoice fees and discounts out of the Labor and Parts columns. PRD version 8 (14 Oct 2026) is later and shares them by side; this case follows the PRD, which we take as prevailing. Which column shows each row's share is on the product owner's question list; judge the amounts wherever they show.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R6: “Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared between the Labor and the Parts rows in proportion to each side's labor or parts dollars after that side's line fees and discounts, measured by size whatever their sign. The adjustment that stops a non-taxable discount from taking the subtotal below zero is a whole-invoice amount and is shared the same way. Example: labor $600.00, parts $400.00, shop supplies $30.00, whole-invoice discount ($50.00). The Labor row gets $30.00 supplies and ($30.00); the Parts row gets ($20.00). Subtotals $600.00 and $380.00 add up to $980.00.”

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), page 4 (cited by the story), export read 19 Oct 2026, used for on-screen labels; the look itself is checked in the "Design — how it looks" cases.
